title: North Carolina midfielder Ashley Sanchez sets U.S. scoring record – USWNT could be next
content:
Ashley Sanchez’s historic NWSL season just keeps getting better.

On Sunday, the North Carolina Courage player scored her 16th regular season goal this year – setting a new league record for most goals scored by an American in a single season. The 27-year-old then scored again, and again, in North Carolina’s 6-0 win over the last-placed Chicago Stars.

Sanchez’s hat trick – the first in her career – also gave her a sizable cushion in the NWSL Golden Boot race. With an impressive 18 goals now scored this season, Sanchez is also closing in on Temwa Chawinga’s single-season record of 20 goals scored in 2024. The Courage still have seven matches to go this season.

North Carolina’s first goal came in the 11th minute, when Sanchez shot a loose ball into an open net after it ricocheted off players in the buildup. The attacking midfielder converted a penalty in the 69th minute for her second and completed her hat trick in the 82nd minute off a header. Another trio of goals came from NWSL rookie Chioma Okafor, Shinomi Koyama and Ryan Williams, helping the club jump from seventh to third in the NWSL standings over the weekend.

“The first goal was probably the easiest goal I’ve ever scored, so that was nice,” a smiling Sanchez said after the game, alongside Okafor. “I feel like I don’t usually get opportunities like that, but, yeah, I just feel like the team came together. We had some really good chances.”

Sanchez’s hat trick came against a Stars team who are currently at the bottom of the league and continue to bury themselves in the standings. Last week, they fell to the Denver Summit 6-1, setting a record for most goals conceded in back-to-back games, according to ESPN. Chicago currently has 16 points across 23 matches played, with a 5-17-1 record. Denver and North Carolina took advantage of the opportunity, with high-scoring games enough to tip the scales in head-to-head comparisons for playoff contention.

North Carolina has accumulated 39 points across 23 matches, with a 12-8-3 record.  To say Sanchez and her incredible season have played a part in the team’s success would be an understatement.

Fans expect Sanchez to be a guaranteed call-up for Emma Hayes in a future U.S. women’s national team camp. The team, after all, has found itself with some glaring holes for this next fall camp against World Cup winner Spain, especially with season-ending injuries sidelining USWNT regulars like Olivia Moultrie and Emily Sonnett.

First-year Courage head coach Mak Lind said he knew coming into the role that Sanchez was an “incredible” player who can play in various positions but is especially productive on the wing.

“This season she has found a couple of keys in her game, which makes her so dangerous offensively. It is not a coincidence that she keeps scoring goals (that) are very important for us,” Lind said. “She has to have herself to thank because she’s an incredible player with attributes. We just helped her with a couple of keys and how to unlock that potential.

“I mean, 18 goals in 23 games is well done in a league like this.”

But Sanchez on Sunday stayed humble. When she was asked if she felt a “career shift” at any point this season, considering her impressive form, she kept the focus on her day-to-day.

“I haven’t really thought about it much,” she said. “I feel like I’m really just enjoying being out there on the field, and I think good things happen when you just put a lot less pressure on yourself. And I have incredible teammates and staff behind me, and I think that’s just helped me improve my game, and – yeah – just enjoy what I’m doing.”
